A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANTS work, and all 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, tables, figures and references. Neither contains appendices or embedded supplements. Separately referenced supplementary material is unavailable, so its contents cannot be compared.

before.justification: v3 reports original ANTS detection results on ImageNet, OpenOOD and other ID datasets, plus component ablations and sensitivity analyses in Tables 1–4 and Figure 7.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experimental results and additionally reports module-level latency measurements in Table 5.

M1.justification: The described negative-image mining, ID-class mining, ENS/VSNL generation and adaptive scoring procedures remain unchanged. The threshold-equation correction and Algorithm 1 cross-reference fixes do not establish a changed implementation or algorithm.

E1.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same ImageNet, OpenOOD and additional ID-dataset coverage, and Figure 7 retains the temporal-shift scenarios. The added latency breakdown uses existing ImageNet coverage. Removing a pointer to unavailable supplementary results does not establish removal of a dataset.

E2.justification: Corresponding detection and complexity comparisons retain the same methods. SynOOD remains in Tables 1 and 2; its Table 1 row moves from the zero-shot group to the training-required group, without changed detection scores or evidence of a revised comparator implementation.

E3.justification: The efficiency evaluation adds separate per-call and amortized per-image measurements for ENS, VSNL, CLIP and other processing. The overall comparison switches from images per second to latency. The stated detection metrics, model configurations and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 5 decomposes inference cost by module, extending the existing complexity analysis to examine MLLM overhead. Table 4 and Figure 7 retain their ablations and robustness analyses. The deleted noisy-negative-image supplementary pointer does not establish removal of the unavailable underlying analysis.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars for the ANTS experiments. The new average latency entries concern amortized processing cost, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Detection results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 6–7 are unchanged. New Table 5 reports ENS/VSNL per-call latencies of 72.55/28.75 ms and per-image averages of 0.18/0.06 ms. The complexity comparison replaces ANTS/EOE throughput of 356/392 images per second with 2.84/2.78 ms; these are not exact reciprocal conversions, and the PDFs do not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Equation 6 changes gamma* from argmax over images to the maximum score, correcting the threshold definition to return a scalar rather than an image. Other mathematical content is retained; merging v3 Equations 10–11 and renumbering subsequent equations are presentation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: ENS and VSNL construction, adaptive weighting, training-free zero-shot operation and state-of-the-art detection claims. The headline performance-improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The complexity discussion now explicitly explains that expensive MLLM calls are selectively triggered and amortized across images, with most samples processed solely by CLIP. Other mechanism explanations and the stated GPU-memory limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds module-level runtime information and clarifies selective MLLM invocation. The default LLaVA model, hyperparameters and RTX 3090 hardware disclosure are retained. The existing repository link moves into the abstract; this does not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: v4 removes several background citations, including GPT-4, Qwen2.5-VL and Generalized ODIN, and adds Qwen3-VL. The related-work taxonomy and principal novelty positioning remain stable. AdaNeg and LAPT publication updates refer to retained works, while SynOOD is newly categorized as training-required in Table 1.

P1.justification: Local edits update affiliations, shorten the algorithm title, correct internal references, rewrite the complexity paragraph and remove two supplementary-material pointers. The section sequence and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds the latency-breakdown table, reformats and renumbers the former complexity table as Table 6, and relocates SynOOD within Table 1. Equation grouping and text reflow change locally. The seven figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves correctness and transparency: Equation 6 now defines a scalar threshold, Algorithm 1 points to the appropriate class-mining equation, and the latency breakdown makes MLLM overhead more assessable. The method and detection evidence remain stable. Unexplained runtime-value changes and unavailable supplementary material limit the strength of the improvement.
